listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Thursday, October 22. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is about PHP. The BBC explains what PHP is and why it set off a global cyber-security scramble. Artificial intelligence uncovered long-hidden programming flaws. That triggered a rare global cyber-security response. If you build software tools, it is worth reading. Now the front page. In basketball, Kevin Durant and Jabari Smith Junior scored thirty points each. The Houston Rockets beat the Dallas Mavericks 128 to 110 in the season opener for both teams. In tech, Claude now works with Google Docs, Sheets and Slides. That is a useful expansion for anyone building workflows around Claude. In world news, the United States ordered some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate. At least three people died in the latest strikes at an airport and an oil field. In politics, AIPAC said it will stop endorsing candidates and giving directly to campaigns. Its affiliated super PAC will continue. Now the sections. In tech, Anthropic released API version 2026-10-21 with new SDK versions. It is also expanding its Cyber Verification Program for qualifying security professionals. And a Cloudflare security audit skill for coding agents is trending on GitHub. In politics, the Justice Department is notifying counties where it wants to monitor elections. Drop Site reports that Iran believes the United States and Israel may strike before the midterms. And The Lever reports on New Hampshire Governor Kelly Ayotte and her shares in Bloom Energy. In world news, Russia freed American Stephen Hubbard after a request from President Trump. Two European aid workers held in Niger for over a year were freed in Libya. And North Korea says it will resume propaganda broadcasts across the border into South Korea. In sports, Raheem Morris returns to Atlanta with a surging 49ers defense. Alexander Volkanovski is preparing for UFC 333. And Khamzat Chimaev wants a rematch with Sean Strickland. In Atlanta, Georgia Tech and Emory announced a joint investment of over one point one billion dollars in AI infrastructure. A new coffee shop is forecast to open on the Beltline in November. And the Michelin Guide to the American South has been released. In architecture, AEC Magazine looks at graphics performance in Revit and AutoCAD. ArchDaily shows a seaside house in Sweden built from brick and wood. It also features a small house in Okayama, Japan. In science, NASA tested an RS-25 engine for future Artemis missions. The Perseverance rover set a new distance record on Mars. And Science News looks at how AI could turn scientific papers into research assistants. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble?
lead.note: A rare global cyber-security response has followed the discovery of long-hidden flaws in PHP. According to the BBC's explainer, artificial intelligence uncovered the programming flaws, and that triggered the scramble. The piece sets out what PHP is and why the discovery set off such a reaction. For a reader who builds software tools, the story matters because it shows a programming technology at the centre of an urgent security effort. It also shows that AI is being used to find weaknesses in code that people had not spotted for a long time. The headline question, what PHP is and why it matters, is one many non-specialists will be asking. The summary does not give technical detail, so the full article is the place to learn how the response worked and what developers are being asked to do.
